office_does: One of two Washington State Representatives for the 48th District (parts of Redmond, Bellevue and Kirkland plus the Points communities and Medina), serving two-year terms writing state law and budgets.
race_blurb: Two Democrats: incumbent Amy Walen, who voted against the 2026 millionaires' tax, and Redmond City Councilmember Jessica Forsythe, backed by the district and county Democrats and the State Labor Council. Forsythe finished 17 votes ahead in the primary.

candidates.summary: State Representative since 2019, chair of Consumer Protection & Business, and former Kirkland mayor; describes herself as a "pragmatic governing Democrat who works across the aisle."
highlights: Voted no on ESSB 6346, the 2026 millionaires' tax, calling it unconstitutional and "not progressive enough" while backing a high-earners income tax in another form [S3][S4]
Prime sponsor of bills enabling commercial-to-housing conversions and limiting historic designations [S3]
Says reproductive options and gender-affirming care "are health care" [S3]
Cites banning ICE agents from wearing masks and sponsoring a bill removing citizenship requirements from most professional licenses [S1][S3]

experience.basis: Seven-year legislator and committee chair with an enacted bill record, plus ten years in Kirkland city government.

taxes.basis: Voted against the millionaires' tax and proposed returning most of its revenue through a sales-tax cut, but says she supports a high-earners income tax and a corporate income tax in place of B&O.

spending.basis: Stresses balanced budgets, the credit downgrade and homelessness-authority oversight, while proposing robust childcare funding and "borrow now" infrastructure investment.

housing.basis: Record emphasizes supply and deregulation (conversions, historic-designation limits, occupancy limits), alongside financing tools for public housing authorities.

local-control.basis: Says she carried cities' concerns on missing-middle policy; The Urbanist reports she voted against statewide middle-housing reform.

safety.basis: Combines police-guild endorsement and support for law enforcement training with gun restrictions, police accountability and crisis-response services.

climate.basis: Voted for the Climate Commitment Act and supports low-carbon fuel standards, alongside an all-sources clean-energy list including nuclear and hydrogen.

immigration.basis: Supported the ICE mask ban and limits on ICE entering schools and hospitals without a warrant; sponsored HB 1889 opening professional licenses to non-citizens.

social.basis: Explicit written support for abortion rights and gender-affirming care as insured health care and for self-determined gender identity; cites backfilling Planned Parenthood funding.

parental-rights.basis: Voted yes on ESHB 1296 and says schools have "an essential role" in comprehensive sexual health education and in protecting children "from unhealthy or abusive families."

candidates.summary: Redmond City Councilmember since 2020 and former Council President; small business owner, SEIU member and former Emerge WA executive director.
highlights: Won tenant protections and $7.5M for housing and human services on the Redmond council [S1]
Pledges to fight for the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, immigrant rights and reproductive freedom [S4]
Endorsed by the 48th and King County Democrats, the State Labor Council and former Gov. Inslee [S1][S5]

experience.basis: Six years of municipal office but no state legislative record, challenging a seven-year incumbent.

housing.basis: Emphasizes deeply affordable housing and renter protections, with a call for more housing at all affordability levels.

climate.basis: Co-wrote a climate emergency declaration and net-zero plan; wants to shift debate from upfront costs to the costs of climate change.

safety.basis: Chaired Redmond's alternative crisis response subcommittee and added mental health professionals to the crisis response team.

spending.basis: Calls K-12 underfunded and wants to fully fund education and reduce reliance on local levies.

immigration.basis: Says she fought for immigrant communities and will fight for immigrant rights.

social.basis: Pledges to fight for the 2SLGBTQIA+ community and reproductive freedom; cites safeguarding reproductive rights.
